subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation / next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity performance validation / next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today — really useful to walk through Acme's production SLOs and workload shape. Recap below and proposed next steps so we can size Dedicated capacity for your targets.

Summary of SLOs and constraints
- Latency: target p95 generation latency <= 200 ms for 512-token avg requests (p50 typically ~60-80ms).
- Throughput: steady-state of ~120 requests/sec, with peak bursts to 220 req/sec for short windows (3-5 minutes).
- Concurrency: expected ~40 concurrent live user streams (each streaming tokens incrementally).
- Streaming: required, with low tail latency for first-byte < 100ms for interactive flows.
- Model: we'll be running open-llm/v1.2 (approx 70B) — please confirm if this exact variant or a quantized variant will be used.
- Typical input sequence length: 350 tokens; output average 160 tokens.

Initial performance notes (from our call)
- Hardware candidates: NVIDIA L4 (cost-efficient), A100 80GB (good FP16 throughput), and H100 (best throughput for 70B with large batch sizes).
- Streaming adds overhead vs batch-only tests — keep KV cache residency and continuous batching in the plan.
- Reserved throughput: we should size for sustained 120 req/s with headroom to 220 in burst mode (autoscale / burst policy).

Proposed validation plan / next steps
1) Test dataset: please share a representative sample of 200 requests (anonymized) with token length distribution. Prefer the file as a gzipped JSONL or CSV.
2) Confirm model binary: open-llm/v1.2 FP16 vs 4-bit quantized variant. This affects GPU selection.
3) Run two quick smoke tests on Dedicated PoC:
   - Config A: 2 x A100-80GB, baseline (FP16) — measure p95 & sustained throughput.
   - Config B: 4 x L4, quantized 4-bit — measure p95 & sustained throughput and cost estimate.
4) We'll instrument traces + per-token latency and share a perf report (PDF) with recommendations (GPU mix, reserved throughput, batch settings).
5) Schedule 2-hour validation window next week; we'll need a point of contact during the run.

Can you confirm: sample payload, model variant, and preferred test window (we suggested Aug 24–26)? Also looping in Marissa and Neha from our infra team to help with test orchestration.

Thanks,
--
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Thanks, Aditya — that looks right. Quick clarifications:
- We'll run the FP16 open-llm/v1.2 binary in prod parity for the validation (no quantized variant for the first run).
- I've attached a 200-sample payload set (anonymized) and the SLO matrix filled out. Please treat the payload as representative; about 20% are long-context (>800 tokens) but most are 300–400 tokens.
- Test window: Aug 25, 09:00–11:00 PT works for us. Carlos will coordinate our infra side and provide a host to collect logs and export token-level traces.

Two asks for your team before the run:
1) Can Redwood provide expected GPU sizing recommendation (A100 vs H100 vs mixed) and a cost delta estimate?
2) For streaming tests, can you confirm how you measure first-byte latency vs end-to-end generation p95? We want clear numbers for both.

Thanks,
Emma
Principal Engineering Manager
Acme Analytics
emma.li@acmeanalytics.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity performance validation / next steps

Marissa / Neha — forwarding Emma's reply and attachments. Key points: FP16 open-llm/v1.2, sample set includes ~20% long-context (>800 tokens), test window Aug 25 09:00–11:00 PT, target sustained 120 req/s with bursts to 220.

Immediate asks for infra planning:
- Based on our experience, start with:
  * Option 1 (latency-priority): 2x H100 (or 2x A100-80GB if H100 not available) pinned to the workload; expected p95 ~120–180ms for 70B FP16 with tuned kernels and continuous batching.
  * Option 2 (cost-priority): 4x L4 with quantization — but Emma said they will run FP16 for first pass, so L4 likely won't hit p95 target for some of their long-context 70B runs.
- Reserve throughput target: configure reserved 140 req/s (sustained) with autoscale to 250 for burst to be safe.
- Streaming: ensure streaming worker warm-up and low first-byte path; measure first-byte separately and instrument via our streaming tracer.

I'll prepare a short perf checklist and our test script commands. Marissa — can you produce a quick cost delta (monthly) for the two options and a recommended starting point? Neha — can you own test orchestration and the tracer config?

Thanks — I will update Emma with our recommended config and cost estimate today.
--
Aditya
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@acmeanalytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity performance validation / next steps

Emma / team — thanks for the payload and matrix. We ran a quick micro-benchmark using a similar 70B FP16 image and preliminary numbers:

Prelim notes (lab run)
- 2x A100-80GB (FP16, tuned kernels) achieved sustained 130 req/s with p95 ~160ms on 512-token gen and first-byte ~85ms. Long-context (>800) pushes p95 closer to 220–260ms.
- 2x H100 shows ~20–30% higher throughput on the same config, with p95 for long-context dropping to ~180–200ms.
- 4x L4 (FP16) struggled on long-context and hit p95 ~350ms; L4 is more cost-effective for smaller models / quantized flows but not ideal here.

Recommendation for validation run (Aug 25, 09:00–11:00 PT)
1) Start with 2x A100-80GB provisioned as Dedicated with reserved 140 req/s and autoscale to 250 for bursts.
2) If H100 is available in your region, recommend trying 2x H100 as a follow-up — throughput headroom, better long-context p95.
3) Instrumentation: we'll enable token-level tracing and streaming-first-byte metrics. We'll provide the tracer snippet and a short dashboard link post-run.

Cost delta (ballpark)
- 2x A100: estimated incremental monthly cost for reserved capacity ~ $35k–$45k.
- 2x H100: ~ $55k–$70k.
- 4x L4: ~ $12k–$16k (but doesn't meet long-context p95).

Next steps
- Aditya: confirm reserved capacity order and test run booking.
- Emma / Carlos: provide an ssh host for logs and confirm POC contact (Carlos?).

Emma — I'll attach the lab perf PDF right after — should help correlate the numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Technical Program Manager, Infra | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
